lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Taylor, this is Daniela. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not great. I haven't been sleeping.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 5 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've picked your days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want your energy back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're already doing things to make it easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've been really tired.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can you do it in the morning instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I need this for my head too, not just my body. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: When I walk I sleep better, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walks after dinner. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to walk 15 minutes on 3 days next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 9. Maybe 10.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 9 and not a 6?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If being so tired gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 5 days, the hard part was being so tired, and next week you're going to walk 15 minutes on 3 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Taylor, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

flags.reason: Coach set a new goal (15 min, 3 days) directly without asking, overriding the participant's own 20-min plan and 3-day commitment.
Asked whether 5 days is realistic right after participant committed to M/W/F, sowing doubt instead of exploring it.
Poor sleep and fatigue were raised repeatedly but not explored; fatigue is linked to the barrier and mood was not checked.

strengths: Line 14 affirmed the participant's effort to make walking easier.
Line 34 and 38 used complex reflections that captured ambivalence and the deeper goal of getting life back.
Line 47 asked an open question about a backup plan for fatigue, and line 49 summarized accurately.
coaching_tips: Line 41: ask permission before setting a goal, e.g., 'Would it help to talk about next week's plan?' and build on the participant's own 20-minute, 3-day plan.
Line 24: replace the doubting question with an open one, such as 'What feels realistic to you for this week?'
Line 4: explore the poor sleep and fatigue before moving to goals, e.g., 'Tell me more about how the sleep has been.'
Line 28 and 32: offer ideas after asking permission and tie them to the participant's stated barriers rather than sequencing several in a row.
Consider setting an agenda early in the call so the participant knows the plan and can shape it.
